testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When does front wheel braking work?
questions.correctAnswerText: Under all conditions.
questions.explanation: Front wheel braking works under all road conditions. Even on ice, front wheels rarely skid.

questions.question: How do you check the automatic transmission fluid level in some vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the engine running.
questions.explanation: In some vehicles, you must leave the engine running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: What happens if a driver does not get an air brakes endorsement?

options.text: They cannot operate a vehicle with air brakes.
They can only operate a vehicle with air brakes for intrastate trips.
They can only operate a vehicle with air brakes for interstate trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot operate a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: To drive a commercial vehicle with air brakes, you must pass the air brakes test and perform your skills test in a vehicle with air brakes.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: They are not allowed on vehicles.
They hold compressed air for the brakes.
They should be drained after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: They hold compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air for the brake system. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of tanks.

questions.question: What should a driver do if they feel tired while driving?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest.
questions.explanation: If you feel drowsy, the only safe choice is to stop and sleep. Stimulants like coffee can be dangerous because fatigue returns suddenly when they wear off.

questions.question: What is an encroachment?

options.text: A driver does not show up for their skills test.
A vehicle touches a boundary line during the skills test.
A driver fails one part of the skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: A vehicle touches a boundary line during the skills test.
questions.explanation: An encroachment happens when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line during the skills test. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: What should you use when driving in fog?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: How does friction happen in an S-cam brake?

options.text: Brake shoes press against the outside of the brake drum.
Brake shoes press against the inside of the brake drum.
Brake shoes push against each other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake shoes press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction happens when brake shoes press against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: What is black ice like?
questions.correctAnswerText: Usually thin.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. It looks like a wet road. Watch for black ice when the road looks wet and the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: What should brake pads have on them?

options.text: No oil, grease, or brake fluid.

questions.correctAnswerText: No oil, grease, or brake fluid.
questions.explanation: When checking your brakes, make sure brake pads have no oil, grease, or brake fluid on them.

questions.question: Which surface is the most slippery?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wet ice
questions.explanation: When the temperature gets slightly warm, ice melts a little and becomes wet. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: During an emergency stop using controlled braking, you should:

options.text: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Press the brakes with about half your normal force.
Press the brakes so the wheels lock up.
Press the brakes with very light pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means pressing the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Keep small steering movements when braking this way.

questions.question: After an accident, flares should be used carefully because:

options.text: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
Other drivers may not see the flares.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
questions.explanation: After an accident, spilled fuel combined with flares can cause a fire.

questions.question: When pulled off on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on the side of the road, use your four-way emergency flashers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: With low beam headlights on, you should be able to see about ____ feet ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Low beam headlights let you see about 250 feet ahead. When driving at night, adjust your speed so you can stop within the distance your headlights illuminate.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, if one air system is very low on pressure:

options.text: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There is usually no noticeable effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, either the front or rear brakes will fail if one air system loses too much pressure. If the air pressure gets too low while driving, pull over and park right away.

questions.question: When entering traffic, you should do everything below except:

options.text: Wait for a large gap between vehicles.
Be ready for your vehicle to accelerate slowly, especially if loaded.
Make sure you can fully cross traffic without interfering with other vehicles.
Assume other drivers will make room for your larger vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers will make room for your larger vehicle.
questions.explanation: Remember your vehicle's size and how much distance it needs to accelerate. Wait for a gap in traffic large enough for your vehicle before accelerating. If your vehicle is heavily loaded, you will need more space to accelerate. Always make sure you can get completely across without interfering with traffic.

questions.question: When starting the engine for the pre-trip inspection, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Listen for unusual noises.
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip inspection, start the engine and listen for any unusual noises.

questions.question: ABS helps you to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in control when stopping.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking during hard braking. Drive and brake the same way with or without ABS.

questions.question: Which is not a good rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Skip your turn signal if you think others know what you plan to do.
Cancel your signal after the turn is completed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip your turn signal if you think others know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when you plan to turn or change lanes. Signal early, keep signaling throughout the turn, and cancel it when done.

questions.question: Loose engine belts will:

options.text: Stop the water pump and fan from working properly, which causes the engine to overheat.
Make the engine run more efficiently.
Make the fan work too hard, causing the engine to become too cold.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the water pump and fan from working properly, which causes the engine to overheat.
questions.explanation: Check your engine belts to make sure they are tight. Loose belts will not work properly and can cause your engine to overheat.

questions.question: After you start the engine, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn off once the vehicle starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off immediately.
questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should turn off right away when the engine starts. This includes the charging circuit, oil, coolant, and anti-lock brake system (ABS) lights.

questions.question: A burning tire should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Cooled with water.
questions.explanation: Cool a burning tire with water. You may need to use a lot of water to cool it properly.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason to use your mirrors?

options.text: You are looking at fuel prices.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are looking at fuel prices.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. You should especially check them when turning, changing lanes, merging, and doing difficult maneuvers.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle driver:

options.text: Can use any cell phone while driving.
Can only use a hands-free cell phone while driving.
Can only use a cell phone on rural roads.
Can use a cell phone at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can only use a hands-free cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: Commercial motor vehicle drivers cannot use hand-held cell phones while driving.

questions.question: Stopping distance can be affected by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your vehicle's speed, its weight, and how much grip the road surface provides.

questions.question: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, the ABS:

options.text: Will still help you steer better.
Will let others see when you brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will still help you steer better.
questions.explanation: When a tractor has ABS but the trailer does not, the ABS will still improve steering control. Watch the trailer and ease off the brakes if it starts to swing out.

questions.question: The application pressure gauge:

options.text: Shows how much air pressure is being sent to the brakes.
Shows the temperature of the air in the braking system.
Shows the pressure of air from the compressor.
Shows how many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shows how much air pressure is being sent to the brakes.
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being sent to the brakes in an air brake system. Not all vehicles with air brakes have this gauge.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, your brakes may fade. What happens when brakes fade?

options.text: They work differently in the front and back.

questions.correctAnswerText: They become less effective.
questions.explanation: Using your brakes too much on a steep downhill can make them overheat and work less well. Use engine braking to avoid overheating your brakes on steep hills.

questions.question: An alcohol evaporator in an air brake system:

options.text: Makes the brakes work without squeaking.
Stops ice from forming in the braking system.
Lubricates parts of the braking system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops ice from forming in the braking system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an evaporator that adds alcohol to the system. The alcohol helps prevent ice from forming inside the braking system.

questions.question: How long does it take for oil pressure to reach normal level when you start a vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: A few seconds
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should reach normal level within a few seconds after starting the engine. Do not drive if oil pressure is low, dropping, or unstable.

questions.question: When driving in wet conditions, no spray from other vehicles' tires means:

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The spray is caught under the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: In wet conditions, no spray from other tires means ice has formed on the road. Drive extra carefully in wet, freezing weather.

questions.question: The ____ shows the driver how much air pressure is in the air tanks.
questions.correctAnswerText: Supply pressure gauge
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a supply pressure gauge. It shows the driver how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: Where must placards be placed on a vehicle carrying hazardous cargo?

options.text: Only on the front of the vehicle.
On the front, rear, and sides of the vehicle.
Only on the driver's side of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, rear, and sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Placards must be on the front, rear, and both sides of vehicles carrying hazardous cargo. They must be visible from every direction.

questions.question: Joggers wearing headsets:

options.text: May not notice what is happening around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not notice what is happening around them.
questions.explanation: Be careful around pedestrians, joggers, and cyclists wearing headphones. They may not hear traffic and may not know you are there.

questions.question: In cold weather, check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator:
questions.correctAnswerText: Every day.
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice buildup in air brake systems. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: When an S-cam turns inside a brake drum, it:

options.text: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Presses the brake shoes against the brake linings.
Presses the brake linings against the wheel axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns and presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: On a power steering-equipped vehicle, the hoses should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Checked for leaks.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a power steering system, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look specifically for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: What information must interstate carriers put on their commercial motor vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: Trade name
questions.explanation: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations require carriers to display the legal name or trade name on each commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: Why should you regularly drain the air tanks?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
To allow for a change in pressure

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains moisture and compressor oil that build up in the air tanks and can damage the brake system. Drain the tanks at the end of each day of driving to remove these materials.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Trust the posted signals to tell you if a train is coming.
Watch what other drivers do to know if a train is coming.
Do not rely only on signals to know if a train is coming.
Look to see if nearby plants are moving from the wind created by a passing train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not rely only on signals to know if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Always approach a railroad crossing as if a train is coming. Do not depend only on signals or sounds to tell you a train is near.

questions.question: When traction is poor, why should a driver accelerate slowly?

options.text: Because it is always good to accelerate slowly.
To keep from losing control of the vehicle.
To keep from going faster than the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep from losing control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate very slowly on slippery roads. Too much power on slippery surfaces can cause you to lose control.

questions.question: If you are driving in fog, you should not:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use your high beam lights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down. Turn on your flashers and low beam headlights.

questions.question: During a vehicle control skills test, where should your vehicle end up?

options.text: In the general area the examiner described.
In the exact spot the examiner described.
Within three feet of where the examiner described.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact spot the examiner described.
questions.explanation: Complete each exercise with your vehicle in the exact position the examiner told you. If you do not finish exactly as described, you can be penalized and may fail the test.

questions.question: What is the number one cause of death and injury in a work zone?
questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers speeding
questions.explanation: Speeding is the leading cause of death and injury in work zones. Be extra careful when driving near workers.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a driving hazard?

options.text: A police car helping a driver on the side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: An open road
questions.explanation: An accident scene is hazardous because people may not watch traffic. Ice cream trucks are hazardous because they attract children who may not notice nearby cars. An open road is not a hazard.

questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?
questions.correctAnswerText: An explosive.
questions.explanation: Explosives are in Class 1 of hazardous materials.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a distraction while driving?
questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your mirrors
questions.explanation: Anything that takes your attention away from driving is a dangerous distraction. This includes eating, drinking, smoking, and adjusting audio or climate controls. Checking your mirrors is part of safe driving.

questions.question: Why should part of your vehicle be visible in a properly adjusted side mirror?

options.text: It limits the view behind the trailer.
It gives you a reference point.
It lets you see stickers on the side of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you a reference point.
questions.explanation: Adjust side mirrors to show part of your vehicle. This helps you judge where nearby objects are.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Do not apply the brakes if the vehicle is left out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park. If needed, also chock the wheels.
